questions.question: Why are rate limits a bigger problem for agents than for chatbots?
options: An agent makes many calls per task (10–100), so limits are hit often and mid-task
Rate limits only apply to agents
questions.explanation: One task fans out into many calls. Without retries and throttling, a single 429 can throw away the whole run.

questions.question: Which response should NOT be retried?
questions.explanation: A 401 means the key is wrong or missing. Retrying sends the same bad key again; fail fast and fix the configuration.

questions.question: A 429 response includes Retry-After: 2. What should the client do?
options: Double the wait to be safe and never retry again
questions.explanation: The server is telling you when capacity frees up. Use its value instead of your own backoff.

questions.question: Why add random jitter to exponential backoff?
options: So many clients that failed together don't all retry at the same moment (thundering herd)
questions.explanation: Without jitter, synchronized clients retry in waves and keep triggering the limit. Randomness spreads them out.

questions.question: Why does load_dotenv refuse a .env file that git isn't ignoring?
options: A .env that git would commit is the most common way keys end up public on GitHub
questions.explanation: Failing before any key is written into a tracked file prevents the leak instead of cleaning up after it.

questions.question: A token bucket allows 5 requests per 10s. You send 7 requests at t=0. When does the 7th start?
questions.explanation: Five burst through at 0s. The bucket refills one token every 2s, so the 6th starts at 2s and the 7th at 4s.
